    The cleopatra preset library, through Digital-Earth¶

    cleopatra 0.31 ships a library of ~200 named parameter presets (cleopatra.styling.colors.DATA_STYLES). Each preset bundles a colormap, a normalization, and a human label tuned for a specific geophysical variable — elevation, sea-surface temperature, radar reflectivity, aerosol optical depth, and so on.

    Digital-Earth exposes the whole library through one keyword: pass style="<preset>" to any raster method (imshow, contourf, pcolormesh, grid_cells, …) and the map picks up that preset's colormap and label. This notebook tours the library; the siblings drill into domains, palettes, and colour scaling.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    %matplotlib inline
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from pyramids.dataset import Dataset
from digitalearth.scene import Map, grid
from cleopatra.styling.colors import DATA_STYLES

DATA = Path('../../../examples/data')   # notebook-relative path (docs/examples/presets -> repo root)
dem = Dataset.read_file(str(DATA / 'LisbonElevation.tif'))   # a small bundled DEM (EPSG:4326)
dem

    What is in the library¶

    Every preset is a named entry cleopatra resolves from DATA_STYLES. They span terrain, weather, ocean, atmospheric-composition and radar families, plus the full set of perceptually-uniform scientific colour maps (batlow, broc, hawaii, davos, …).

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    presets = sorted({sub for v in DATA_STYLES.values() if isinstance(v, dict) for sub in v})
print(len(presets), 'presets available')
print('examples:', presets[:16])
    presets = sorted({sub for v in DATA_STYLES.values() if isinstance(v, dict) for sub in v}) print(len(presets), 'presets available') print('examples:', presets[:16])
    201 presets available
examples: ['acton', 'aerosol_optical_depth_550nm', 'air_temperature', 'anomaly', 'aod', 'bam', 'bamO', 'bamako', 'bathymetry', 'batlow', 'batlowK', 'batlowW', 'berlin', 'bilbao', 'broc', 'brocO']

    One field, many presets¶

    The quickest way to feel the library is to render the same elevation field under a spread of presets. digitalearth.scene.grid lays out a grid of shared-CRS maps; each panel just calls imshow(dem, style=...).

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    show = ['elevation', 'bathymetry', 'batlow', 'hawaii', 'broc',
        'davos', 'grayC', 'temperature', 'anomaly']
fig, maps = grid(3, 3, crs=dem.epsg, figsize=(13, 11))
for m, preset in zip(maps, show):
    m.imshow(dem, style=preset)
    m.set_title(preset)
fig;
    show = ['elevation', 'bathymetry', 'batlow', 'hawaii', 'broc', 'davos', 'grayC', 'temperature', 'anomaly'] fig, maps = grid(3, 3, crs=dem.epsg, figsize=(13, 11)) for m, preset in zip(maps, show): m.imshow(dem, style=preset) m.set_title(preset) fig;

    A preset carries its label¶

    A preset is more than a colormap — it also knows what it is plotting. Rendering one on its own and adding a colorbar shows the preset's colormap and its label together.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=dem.epsg, figsize=(9, 7))
m.imshow(dem, style='elevation')
m.colorbar(label='elevation (m)')
m.set_title("style='elevation'")
m.fig;
    m = Map(crs=dem.epsg, figsize=(9, 7)) m.imshow(dem, style='elevation') m.colorbar(label='elevation (m)') m.set_title("style='elevation'") m.fig;

    Presets are just a keyword — the next notebooks pair them with matching data (02_domain_presets), show the palette builders behind them (03_palettes_and_colormaps), and drive the colour scaling and terrain shading (04_color_scaling_and_terrain).
